1. journald-cap  [safe]  fixes LOG-001
   Cap the persistent journal at 1G with a journald drop-in
   create   /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-stackward-journal-cap.conf (0644)
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-stackward-journal-cap.conf
            @@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step journald-cap, fixes LOG-001.
            +# Caps the persistent journal. Remove this file and restart
            +# systemd-journald to undo.
            +[Journal]
            +SystemMaxUse=1G
   run      systemctl restart systemd-journald
            # load the new limit; journald vacuums older files down to it
   restarts systemd-journald
   note     Restarting systemd-journald drops no running service; journal files older than the 1G limit are deleted.
   undo     Remove the drop-in and restart systemd-journald; the journal may then grow to the default limit again. Journal files already vacuumed are gone.
            rm -f /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-stackward-journal-cap.conf
            systemctl restart systemd-journald

2. sysctl-hardening  [safe]  fixes KRN-002, KRN-003, KRN-004
   Set the kernel hardening values with a sysctl drop-in
   create   /etc/sysctl.d/90-stackward-hardening.conf (0644)
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/sysctl.d/90-stackward-hardening.conf
            @@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step sysctl-hardening, fixes KRN-002, KRN-003, KRN-004.
            +# Hardening values only: net.ipv4.ip_forward and the other settings
            +# Docker needs are never set here. Remove this file to undo at the
            +# next boot.
            +net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 2
            +net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
            +kernel.kptr_restrict = 1
   run      sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/90-stackward-hardening.conf
            # apply this drop-in now, and only this file, not the whole sysctl.d tree
   note     /etc/sysctl.conf sets kernel.kptr_restrict = 0 and is read after this drop-in, so the old value returns at boot; change it there by hand.
   note     /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=0 (want 1) and ufw applies it again on every enable and reload; this step leaves that file alone.
   undo     Remove the drop-in so the old values return at the next boot, and set the old running values now.
            rm -f /etc/sysctl.d/90-stackward-hardening.conf
            sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=1
            sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=1
            sysctl -w kernel.kptr_restrict=0
